podcast.body: The third track from "The Joshua Tree" and a surprising choice for a single, given its downbeat nature compared to U2's more energetic earlier hits. Despite this, it became a favorite among the band's office staff and others during its creation. The track features The Edge playing the "infinite sustain guitar," an instrument invented by Michael Brook in Toronto and delivered to Dublin, which The Edge recorded in just two takes. "It just started becoming everybody's favorite song and some of the folks from the U2 office and people hang around always gravitated to it and they said that's something very special about that."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song is one of dozens based on the same four-chord progression (E, B, C#, A), demonstrating how common musical structures are reused in popular music. "all these songs are constructed around those chords."

podcast.body: This song was mentioned as coming together "very quickly" and was already "quite formed" before its recording. It served as the A-side for "Luminous Times (Hold on to Love)" and had "Mothers of the Disappeared" as a B-side in Guatemala. "With or without you came very quickly. You know, it was already quite formed."
